Sunlight contains all colors, but as it passes through the atmosphere, shorter wavelengths (blue and violet) are scattered much more strongly by nitrogen and oxygen molecules than longer wavelengths (red and orange) — a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering. Although violet scatters even more than blue, our eyes are more sensitive to blue and the Sun emits less violet light, so the scattered light we perceive across the sky appears predominantly blue.
